newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schwarz Pharma says profits to grow in 97.
newsitem.headline: Schwarz Pharma says profits to grow in 97.

text.p: German drugs group Schwarz Pharma AG, forecasting a 15 percent rise in 1996 sales and profits, said next year's profits would grow more strongly than sales, which are slated to rise between six and eight percent.
"Even in the coming years, we do not need to be worried about the development of profits," Patrick Schwarz-Schuette, chairman of the family-owned group, told a news conference.

After reporting a 22.7 percent rise in nine-month sales to 885.7 million marks ($567.8 million) and pre-tax profits of 138.7 million marks, Schwarz-Schuette said full year profits and sales would show a 15 percent rise, meeting targets set earlier this year.
Sales for 1996 were forecast to total 1.18 billion marks and earnings per share, calculated according to the German DVFA accounting rules, should also rise 15 percent to 4.30 marks, the company said.
Strong results should allow the group to raise its 1996 dividend payout on shares initially floated last year, by 20 percent to 1.50 marks per share, Schwarz-Schuette said.

Sales growth was largely driven by acquisitions as Schwarz Pharma entered a number of joint-ventures abroad to diversify its operations geographically. Stripping out takeovers, 1996 sales would have climbed 6.8 percent, the group said.
Looking ahead Schwarz-Schuette said cost reductions, including lower administrative costs, should help profits grow more strongly than sales.

Internal growth should push sales to up to 1.7 billion marks in the next four to five years, Schwarz-Schuette said, explaining that additional sales from possible acquisitions would be added onto these figures.
New products should contribute additional sales of 250 to 300 million marks, the group said, adding that sales prospects for an impotence drug and a blood-pressure drug were particularly promising.
The group expects to have a number of smaller new drug launches as well as periodic updating of older drugs.
On the bourse, where Schwarz Pharma has been a favourite since its flotation last year, the outlook was rewarded with a 3.5 percent rise in the share price taking it to 113.90 marks.
Schwarz Pharma shares have climbed 115 percent in value since the listing, but Schwarz-Schuette said the group has no plans to float more shares in the near term.
The group, eager to buy promising research rather than conduct all the research itself, said it was actively looking for takeover candidates but would not blindly buy any company.
"We are actively looking for companies, but initially no such takeover is on the horizon," Schwarz-Schuette said.
A current goal could be to strengthen the group's sales network in France, Italy, Spain or the United States.
Financing such cooperation would be relatively comfortable considering the group's 180 million mark cash flow, Schwarz Pharma's chief financial officer Klaus Peter Langer said.
"Our war chest consists of about two billion marks," Schwarz-Schuette said. --Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525 ($ = 1.559 German Marks)
